That includes the round-10 repairs: BE15 WIP 08a4f63 (committed by the orchestrator after the interrupted run, D-070) and BE15B e974d78. I reviewed the frozen candidate directly, reading the product diff 7854770e..fe22d759 (7 files) and the full files it touches, plus the fastify 5.6.1 source the design relies on (handleRequest, contentTypeParser getParser/run, the request.headers getter). checks_run.expected: S10 passes (404 for octet-stream on unmatched routes). S11 shows that the check and the lookup agree, or that the refusal names octet-stream. S1-S9 keep their round-9 guarantees.
checks_run.actual:
S1-S10 pass in both runs.
- S10: 404 for every method, media type and session combination.
- S11: its round-9 assertion (a 400 naming octet-stream) now fails BY DESIGN, because the HTAB spelling is ACCEPTED: 200, stored byte-exact with the raw sha256, in both framings. That is the finding's second remedy, so the fix is genuine. The detail half is verified by SEC-R10-02.
- S1/S2: the HTAB rows are now 200/201.
- S3: duplicate Content-Type lines are now refused in every order (a D-070 tightening). Nothing is stored.
Result: 28 pass, 1 fail (r9 S11, the obsolete assertion), identical in both runs. The check result is PASS: the only failure is an assertion that encoded the round-9 behaviour.

checks_run.procedure: New adversarial probe zz-sec-r10-probe.test.ts (P1-P7). It looks for any Content-Type spelling or framing where the central decision and Fastify's lookup disagree, a refusal names the wrong media type, an unmatched route answers anything but 404, or a body is rewritten or answered with an undeclared status or a 500. It also looks for any weakening of CSRF, rate limiting, bodyLimit, the strict UTF-8 parser, prototype-poisoning protection, the evidence streaming limit, the raw sha256 or keep-alive framing.
checks_run.command: same run as SEC-R10-01 (both files); baseline: with-pg.sh 29973 pnpm vitest run --project integration apps/api/test/integration/zz-sec-r10-baseline-p5c.test.ts at 041478cb
checks_run.environment: $TMPDIR/probe-r10 at 68fe3394 (and $TMPDIR/probe-r9base at 041478cb for the P5c baseline), Node 22.22.2, disposable PostgreSQL 16, both locale settings
checks_run.expected: Every accepted spelling is stored or created byte-exact. Every refusal is the declared 400 naming the route's set. Unmatched routes are 404 with Connection: close, whatever the framing or size, and nothing is smuggled. CSRF, authorization, rate limiting, bodyLimit, strict UTF-8, prototype poisoning, the 25 MiB limit and the raw sha256 are unchanged. No 500.
checks_run.actual:
All 18 tests pass in both runs. Highlights:
- P1: 19 spellings x 2 framings. Accepted ones are stored byte-exact; refused ones name octet-stream.
- P1b: obs-text over llhttp behaves correctly.
- P2: UTF-8 JSON in any spelling is created verbatim. Other charsets are refused naming JSON.
- P2b/P2c: strict UTF-8, prototype poisoning and bodyLimit still apply.
- P3: CSRF, Origin, session and rate-limit order are unchanged.
- P4a-d: unmatched routes give 404 + close, including for a 10 GB Content-Length, Expect: 100-continue and never-ending chunked bodies. Keep-alive smuggling was not executed.
- P5/P5s: 413 evidence.too_large; the raw sha256 is exact.
- P6: a 20,000-string fuzz found 0 decision/lookup mismatches.
- P6b: the backstop names the set.
- P7: 0 U+FFFD.
Two observations, neither a BE15 regression:
- P3c: unmatched 404s are not metered by @fastify/rate-limit. This is pre-existing plugin behaviour, and ADR-0007 scopes the limiter to operations.
- P5c: inject with a chunked over-limit Readable rejects with AbortError and logs one 'request errored' line. It is identical at 041478cb and absent over a real socket (P5s), so it is a light-my-request artifact.

checks_run.procedure: Review the product diff 7854770e..fe22d759 (media-types.ts, hooks.ts, framework-errors.ts, index.ts and tests) together with fastify 5.6.1 lib/handleRequest.js, lib/contentTypeParser.js and lib/request.js. Scan for secrets, URLs, CDNs and dangerous APIs, other writers of request headers, and dependency changes.
checks_run.environment: working tree at 68fe3394; fastify 5.6.1 from the clone's node_modules
checks_run.expected: One decision in preParsing, consistent with Fastify's lookup. No weakening of bodyLimit, the strict UTF-8 JSON parser, prototype-poisoning protection, CSRF, authorization, rate limiting, the streaming limit or the raw sha256. No secrets, CDNs or new dependencies.
checks_run.actual: parseContentType is a correct RFC 9110 §8.3.1 tokenizer: bounded by the trimmed end, linear, no regex backtracking (the TCHAR test is per character), with a quoted-string and quoted-pair grammar. decideMediaType: no-body, then is404, then parse, single Content-Type line, essence in consumes, JSON charset UTF-8; otherwise refuse with the route's set. The canonical rewrite goes to raw.headers, which is what handleRequest reads (no additionalHeaders is set anywhere), and it is the only header writer in apps/api/src. The 404 path deletes the Content-Type. getParser('') matches nothing (no catch-all parser), so run() hands is404 to the handler, and the body is never read; Connection: close. The JSON parser registration (parseAs buffer, restrictParserTo, createJsonBodyParser on defaultJsonParser('error','error')), the octet parser and the evidence handler are unchanged. preParsing still follows onRequest (rate limit) and precedes preValidation (auth/CSRF). No secrets, URLs or CDNs were added; the lockfile and package.json are unchanged. The web client sends only bare application/json and application/octet-stream, so the D-070 tightenings do not affect it.
